title: Classify support tickets responsibly
description: Define allowed categories, confidence thresholds and human handoff.
accomplishes: Define allowed categories, confidence thresholds and human handoff. Separate urgency from sentiment and avoid sensitive profiling. Provide labelled synthetic examples, correction rules and monitoring. Do not close tickets or send customer replies automatically without authorisation.
prompt:
Act as an automation architect.

Task: Classify support tickets responsibly.

Input context:
- TICKET TYPES: [TICKET TYPES]
- LABELS: [LABELS]
- PRIORITIES: [PRIORITIES]
- ESCALATION: [ESCALATION]

Define allowed categories, confidence thresholds and human handoff. Separate urgency from sentiment and avoid sensitive profiling. Provide labelled synthetic examples, correction rules and monitoring. Do not close tickets or send customer replies automatically without authorisation.

Keep secrets server-side, minimise data and require human approval for consequential or external actions. Include idempotency and controlled recovery.

Use English for explanations unless the task or user explicitly requires another language. Use clear sections and a format suited to the deliverable. If essential information is missing, ask a focused question before concluding. Label assumptions and unknowns. Do not invent facts, sources, results or completed checks. End with verification criteria and remaining limitations.
exampleResult:
## Support routing proposal
A login-access issue goes to the account-support queue; a billing discrepancy requires a reviewer with appropriate access. Ambiguous tickets retain an “Uncertain” state. Staff can correct labels and inspect the reason. Track misroutes instead of assuming high model confidence means correctness. No actual customer ticket is read, closed or answered here.
